## Photolysis rate constants (`type: photolysis`) {#sec-ch07-rate}

### Summary

The photolysis rate constant of a reaction is the number of dissociations per molecule per second. It is the
cross section of the dissociation channels times the actinic flux, integrated over wavelength. kintera evaluates the
integral with the trapezoidal rule on the cross-section grid, or as a weighted sum when quadrature weights are given
(for a flux already integrated over each bin). The absorption branch does not count towards the rate.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $J = \int \sigma_d(\lambda, T)\, F(\lambda)\, \mathrm d\lambda$, @eq-ch07-rate-integral.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $F$ on the grid; returns $J$ [$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$] per reaction.

**Placement.** `update_xs_diss_stacked(T)` when $T$ changes, then `forward(T, F)`.

**Activation.** `type: photolysis`; the option `quadrature_weights` (API, no YAML key) selects a weighted sum; default trapezoidal.

**Guarantee / limits.** Second-order trapezoidal rule in $\lambda$; no unit conversion inside.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $J$, photolysis rate constant [$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$]; $\sigma_d$, dissociative cross section
[$\mathrm{cm^2\,molecule^{-1}}$]; $\sigma$, absorption cross section [$\mathrm{cm^2\,molecule^{-1}}$]; $q_b$, quantum
yield of channel $b$ [-]; $\sigma_b = \sigma q_b$, partial cross section of branch $b$; $\sigma_{\mathrm{nd}}$, the non-dissociating part of the absorption [$\mathrm{cm^2\,molecule^{-1}}$]; $J_b$, rate of channel $b$
[$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$]; $w_i$, quadrature weight of grid point $i$ [nm, or 1 for pre-binned flux]; $\lambda_i$, grid
wavelengths [nm].

### Derivation

**Counting photons.** Let $F(\lambda)\,\mathrm d\lambda$ be the number of photons with wavelength in
$[\lambda, \lambda + \mathrm d\lambda]$ that cross a unit area per second, summed over all directions (the actinic
flux of @sec-ch07-actinic-flux). A molecule with absorption cross section $\sigma(\lambda, T)$ intercepts the area
$\sigma$ of that stream, so it absorbs $\sigma F\,\mathrm d\lambda$ photons per second in the interval. Each absorbed
photon dissociates the molecule into channel $b$ with probability $q_b(\lambda, T)$, the quantum yield of the
channel, and leaves it undissociated with probability $q_0 = 1 - \sum_{b \ge 1} q_b$. The rate of channel $b$ per
molecule is therefore

$$
J_b = \int \sigma\, q_b\, F\, \mathrm d\lambda = \int \sigma_b\, F\, \mathrm d\lambda ,
\qquad \sigma_b \equiv \sigma\, q_b ,
$$

so a branch column of the deck (@sec-ch07-cross-sections) is a partial cross section, absorption times yield, and
the reader never needs $\sigma$ and $q_b$ separately.

**Column convention.** kintera's cross-section columns follow one convention for every format: column 0 holds the
total absorption cross section $\sigma_0 = \sigma$, and columns $b \ge 1$ hold the dissociation channels $\sigma_b =
\sigma q_b$. The part of the absorption that leaves the molecule intact is not stored; it is

$$
\sigma_{\mathrm{nd}} = \sigma_0 - \sum_{b \ge 1} \sigma_b = \sigma\, q_0 ,
$$

which is non-negative only if the yields sum to at most 1. This is the convention of row K18 on the code-fix
tracker.[^ch07-k18-convention] At the pin two parts of the code do not follow it: the KINETICS7 reader stores
$\sigma_{\mathrm{nd}}$ in column 0 (@eq-ch07-cross-sections-absorption), and `get_effective_stoich` weights branch 0 by
$\sigma_0$ instead of $\sigma_{\mathrm{nd}}$ (@sec-ch07-photochem).

**Only dissociation counts.** The photolysis rate constant is the number of molecules destroyed per molecule per
second, the sum of the channel rates,

$$
J = \sum_{b \ge 1} J_b = \int \sigma_d(\lambda, T)\, F(\lambda)\, \mathrm d\lambda ,
\qquad \sigma_d(\lambda, T) = \sum_{b \ge 1} \sigma_b(\lambda, T) .
$$ {#eq-ch07-rate-dissociative}

Column 0 is the total absorption, and its composition is the reactant (@sec-ch07-cross-sections). Including it would
count every dissociating photon twice and also count the absorptions that leave the molecule intact, so it is left
out of $\sigma_d$. When a reaction has only one branch, the code uses
that branch as $\sigma_d$. @eq-ch07-rate-dissociative is computed in `update_xs_diss_stacked`
({{< code src/photochem/photolysis.cpp PhotolysisImpl::update_xs_diss_stacked >}}). Nothing in the code checks
$\sum_{b \ge 1} q_b \le 1$, that is $\sigma_d \le \sigma$; the deck is trusted.

**The trapezoid on the cross-section grid.** The integral is evaluated on the grid $\lambda_1 < \dots < \lambda_N$ of
the cross sections. On each interval the integrand is replaced by the straight line through its end values, which
gives

$$
J = \int \sigma_d(\lambda, T)\, F(\lambda)\, \mathrm d\lambda
\approx \sum_{i=1}^{N-1} \frac{\lambda_{i+1} - \lambda_i}{2}
\left[\sigma_d(\lambda_i) F(\lambda_i) + \sigma_d(\lambda_{i+1}) F(\lambda_{i+1})\right] ,
$$ {#eq-ch07-rate-integral}

computed in `forward` ({{< code src/photochem/photolysis.cpp PhotolysisImpl::forward >}}) by `torch::trapezoid`
over the wavelength axis. Collecting the terms of each node writes the same sum as $\sum_i w_i \sigma_d(\lambda_i)
F(\lambda_i)$ with the weights

$$
w_1 = \frac{\lambda_2 - \lambda_1}{2} ,\qquad
w_i = \frac{\lambda_{i+1} - \lambda_{i-1}}{2}\ \ (1 < i < N) ,\qquad
w_N = \frac{\lambda_N - \lambda_{N-1}}{2} :
$$

an interior node carries half of each neighbouring interval, the two end nodes only half of their one interval. The
grid need not be uniform. Nothing is added outside $[\lambda_1, \lambda_N]$: flux beyond the table does not
contribute, however large it is.

**Pre-binned flux.** When the caller sets `quadrature_weights`, `forward` uses its own weights instead,

$$
J = \sum_i w_i\, \sigma_d(\lambda_i)\, F(\lambda_i) ,
$$ {#eq-ch07-rate-weighted}

also computed in `forward` ({{< code src/photochem/photolysis.cpp PhotolysisImpl::forward >}}). If $F_i$ is the flux
already integrated over bin $i$, in photons $\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ per bin, and $\sigma_d(\lambda_i)$ stands for
the bin, unit weights give $J = \sum_i \sigma_d(\lambda_i) F_i$, the per-bin sum.

**Units.** In @eq-ch07-rate-integral, $\mathrm{cm^2} \times \mathrm{photons\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,nm^{-1}} \times
\mathrm{nm} = \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. The code converts none of the three, so $\sigma$ must be in
$\mathrm{cm^2\,molecule^{-1}}$, $F$ in $\mathrm{photons\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,nm^{-1}}$ and $\lambda$ in nm; any other
consistent set (for example SI throughout) gives the same $J$, a mixed set does not.

**Check.** The script `derivation-checks/check_ch07_photolysis.py` builds one reaction with two product channels and
branch 0 on the non-uniform grid (100, 115, 150, 160, 200) nm, with two temperature slabs, and evaluates `forward`
at three temperatures, one inside and two outside the slabs.[^ch07-check-rate] Its lines are

```text
[a1] max rel |J - trapezoid(sum_{b>=1} sigma_b F)| at T = 250, 180, 340 K: 1.110e-16 (tol 1e-13) PASS
[a2] J / J(branch 0 included) = 0.4348: branch 0 does not count towards J INFO
[b] rel |J(cgs, nm) - J(SI: area m2, flux per m2 per s per m of wavelength, wavelength m)|: 1.110e-16 (tol 1e-13) PASS
```

`[a1]` is @eq-ch07-rate-integral with the end-node weights above, `[a2]` shows that branch 0 is left out (including
it would raise $J$ by the factor 1/0.4348), and `[b]` re-evaluates the integral in SI units. The weighted sum
@eq-ch07-rate-weighted is checked by the run in the Numerical method layer, not by the script.
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch07-rate-dissociative check_ch07_photolysis.py [a2] -->
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch07-rate-integral check_ch07_photolysis.py [a1] -->

### Numerical method

`update_xs_diss_stacked` interpolates every reaction to the current temperature and caches $\sigma_d$ as one
(batch, wavelength, reaction) tensor. `forward` refuses to run on an empty or mismatched cache, multiplies by the
flux (moving a leading wavelength dimension of the flux to the back) and integrates over the wavelength dimension.
The trapezoidal rule is second order in the grid spacing for a smooth integrand; the grid is the cross-section grid,
so its accuracy depends on how well that grid resolves $\sigma F$ (not measured).

Axes: the cache holds $\sigma_d$ with shape `(*T.shape, nwave, nreaction)` (from the header comment), and `forward`
returns $J$ with shape `(*T.shape, nreaction)`. The leading axes are the batch axes of the temperature tensor; a flux of shape `(nwave)` is
broadcast over them, and a flux of shape `(nwave, *T.shape)` is moved to wavelength-last before the product. These shapes
were checked by the caller-contract run of @sec-ch07-actinic-flux.

Verified by a run against kintera 2.6.5 built from the pin[^ch07-rate-src]: for a reaction with dissociation
branch $\sigma_1 = (1, 2, 4) \times 10^{-18}$ on $\lambda = (100, 150, 200)$ nm and a uniform $F = 10^{14}$, `forward`
returns $J = 0.0225\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$, the trapezoidal value of the dissociation branch alone; unit weights return
$7.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}} = \sum_i \sigma_1 F$.

The figure of the integrand is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of the photolysis rate constants. {#tbl-ch07-rate-code}

Refused: `forward` before `update_xs_diss_stacked`; a flux whose first dimension is not the grid size; a cache built
for another grid or reaction count; weights whose size differs from the grid.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|

| check (`check_ch07_photolysis.py`) | @eq-ch07-rate-integral on a non-uniform grid at three temperatures; branch 0 excluded; SI re-evaluation (`[a1]`, `[a2]`, `[b]`) | $10^{-13}$ rel. | round-off |

: Tests of the photolysis rate constants. {#tbl-ch07-rate-tests}

No registered test compares $J$ with a closed form or checks the weighted sum. The check script is not a registered
test; the weighted sum is checked only by the run in the Numerical method layer.

### Limits

An absorption-only reaction (one branch) gets $J$ from its absorption branch; its products equal its reactants, so
the net tendency is zero, but the rate is not (from reading `update_xs_diss_stacked`).
